newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka rebels say will swap prisoners for men.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka rebels say will swap prisoners for men.

text.p: Tamil Tiger separatists said on Tuesday they would release villagers they had abducted in eastern Sri Lankan only if the military freed rebels captured in the same area.

The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels captured 39 Moslem and Sinhala men from the village of Erakkandi in Trincomalee district last month after the village handed over to the military some guerrillas who had escaped a sea battle.
Seven of the villagers were released on Monday after the International Committee of the Red Cross negotiated their return.

The clandestine Voice of Tiger radio, monitored in government-held Vavuniya, some 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo, said the LTTE were ready to swap the remaining 32 prisoners for their own men held by the military.
A military spokesman in Colombo declined comment.
The radio quoted a statement from the political wing of LTTE, which has been fighting a 13-year-old war for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east.

"There was a boat accident in the Trincomalee sea and our cadres swam across many miles to reach the village. They were unarmed and asked for help from the villagers. But the villagers inhumanly attacked our cadres and handed them over to the Sri Lankan military," the radio said.
"As a result of this incident we were forced to capture 39 villagers and detain them," it added.
The two communities have clashed in the past and at least eight Moslems and three Tamils were killed in communal violence in the east last January.

"We consider Moslems as our brothers and we have no plan to harm them," the radio said. But it warned the community that the rebels were disturbed by last month's incident and said it should not be repeated.
Separately, military officials in the east said three soldiers were killed early on Tuesday when the rebels ambushed a foot patrol at Valaichchenai in Batticaloa district.
The government says 50,000 people have been killed in the war. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
